titleStmt.title: History of the Zhou Dynasty · Western Zhou 西周

div.interp: 公将不利于孺子: the Metal-bound Coffer of the Documents, after Legge, "the duke would do no good to the (king's) young son".
匽: the form of 燕, Yan, in the bronze inscriptions.
顽民: Legge's rendering in the Charge to the Duke of Bi of the Documents, 毖殷顽民，迁于洛邑, "Cautiously did he deal with the refractory people of Yin, and removed them to the city of Lo".
昜: so written in a bronze inscription of the early Western Zhou, 王命昜伯侯于晋，唯王廿又八祀; the transmitted texts have Tang 唐.
刑错: 错 is read as 措, to lay aside (Ying Shao, in the Jijie).
荆: Jing, the name by which the inscriptions and the old texts call Chu.
过伯簋: translated with Robert Eno's version at hand (Inscriptional Records of the Western Zhou, no. 39), which has "Elder of Guo" and "clan shrine". 白 and 乍 are the inscription's forms of 伯 and 作.
丧六师于汉: after Legge's translation of the Bamboo Annals, "The king's six armies perished in the Han".
班簋: translated after Robert Eno (Inscriptional Records of the Western Zhou, no. 46), who has "bring peace to the eastern lands" and "none do not submit".
密: the state of Mi, traditionally placed at Lingtai, Gansu, on the land of the former Mixu.
王室遂衰，戎狄交侵，暴虐中国: the words of the Hanshu, Account of the Xiongnu.
右扶风槐里，周曰犬丘，懿王都之: the entry for Huaili in the Hanshu, Treatise on Geography.

敔簋: translated with Robert Eno's version at hand (Inscriptional Records of the Western Zhou, no. 103), which takes 上洛 as the upper reaches of Luo River and dates the vessel to King Li. 尸 is the inscription's form of 夷.
厉王无道，淮夷入寇，王命虢仲征之，不克: the words of the Hou Hanshu, Account of the Eastern Yi; 熊渠畏其伐楚，亦去其王 are those of the Shiji, Hereditary House of Chu.
荒服: the outermost of the five domains in the Tribute of Yu of the Documents, in Legge "the Wild domain".
厉王既亡，有共伯和者摄行天子事: the Bamboo Annals as the Jinshu, Biography of Shu Xi, reports it, where the received text has 幽王 for 厉王.
秦仲立三年: the paragraph is the text of the Shiji, Basic Annals of Qin.
共和十四年: 827 BC.
宣王即位…: the first sentence is the text of the Shiji, Basic Annals of Zhou; what follows is drawn from the Basic Annals of Qin.
江汉: Legge's translation, with the names in pinyin: the first stanza, and from the third the King's charge.
常武: Legge's translation of the last stanza, with the names in pinyin.
采芑: Legge's translation of the last stanza, with the names in pinyin.
三十二年: 795 BC, with King Xuan's first year at 826 BC.
三十九年: 788 BC.
四十六年: 781 BC.
宣王征申戎后十年…伯士死焉: the text of the Hou Hanshu, Account of the Western Qiang.
邾娄: the Gongyang Zhuan's form of 邾, Zhu.
召旻: the first two stanzas are Legge's translation; the last is rendered with his notes on it, which give "to open up", "contracted" and "men of the old virtue".
曾, 缯, 鄫: three ways of writing the one name, Zeng.
二王并立: the words of the Bamboo Annals, as quoted in the Zhengyi to the Zuozhuan under Duke Zhao's twenty-sixth year: 周二王并立.
幽王败亡后二年…四年: the reckoning of Chen Zan in the commentary to the Hanshu, Treatise on Geography: 幽王既败，二年而灭会，四年而灭虢, where 会 is Kuai 郐.
邢侯大破北戎: the words of the Hou Hanshu, Account of the Western Qiang.
战于长丘: the defeat of the Di at Changqiu and the taking of Yuansi are told in the Zuozhuan under Duke Wen's eleventh year, as of the time of Duke Wu of Song.

宗周九年无王: the Xinian of the Tsinghua slips has 周亡王九年, "Zhou was without a king for nine years", and after it the meeting at Shao'e, the setting up at Jingshi and, three years later, the move east to Chengzhou. Zongzhou 宗周 is the name of the western capital, Hao.
佐周平戎，甚有功: the words of the Shiji, Hereditary House of Kangshu of Wey.
